title: Fluid reading, voiceless texts, digits, ruqʿa

blocks.text: You know all the letters and signs: this unit leads you from deciphering to reading. You learn to break prefixes and suffixes, read titles without vowels, use Arabic numerals, recognize handwriting more widely (ruqʿa) and to write with the full keyboard. Finally there is the Level exam 0.

rows: 6–7 hours · one week (week 11 of the calendar)

blocks.text: Materials This unit, calligraphy L0-10, Anki deck (tag L0-10), stopwatch
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. recognise and separate the most frequent prefixes and suffixes;
2. read short titles without vowels with well-known words, declaring ambiguities;
3. read a new vocalized text of 40 words at least 20 words per minute;
4. read and write Arabic and Indo-Arabic figures and dates;
5. recognize the words notes written in ruqʿa;
6. type any word on the Arabic keyboard.
Plan of the week.
7 General review for the exam (week) 12)
Many Arabic words are actually a word plus one or more attached elements. Before searching for a word in the dictionary or translating it, separate them. More frequent prefixes.

blocks.text: A writing rule. ⁧لِ⁩ + ⁧الـ⁩ lose the article's alif: write ⁧لِلْحُكُومَةِ⁩ , not ⁧لالحكومة⁩ ». More frequent suffixes.

A writing rule. In front of a suffix ⁧ة⁩ becomes ⁧ت⁩ : ⁧مَدِينَة⁩ → ⁧مَدِينَتِي⁩ madīnatī My city is. Personal suffixes are studied in A1-09 and A2-10: Now you just recognize them so as not to confuse them with the word.
With vowels read letter by letter; without vocal laws recognizing. Proceed like this:
1. Remove prefixes and suffixes (section 1).
2. Use long letters. ⁧ا و ي⁩ indicates long or diphthong vowels: they are the backbone of the word.
3. Recognize frequent words at a glance: ⁧في، من، إلى، على، هذا، مع، بعد⁩ . You store them with Anki.
4. Use context to choose from multiple readings ( ⁧دين، كتب، عمل، سجن⁩ ).
5. He's declaring uncertainty. If two readings change the way and context does not decide, in a professional job You write it down.

2.3 The first continuous text
⁧اليَوْمَ⁩ . ⁧فِي المَدِينَةِ جَامِعَاتٌ وَمَطَارَاتٌ وَبُيُوتٌ كَثِيرَةٌ⁩ . ⁧مِيلَانُو مَدِينَةٌ كَبِيرَةٌ فِي شَمَالِ إِيطَالِيَا⁩

⁧اليوم⁩ . ⁧في المدينة جامعات ومطارات وبيوت كثيرة⁩ . ⁧ميلانو مدينة كبيرة في شمال إيطاليا⁩

Grammatical note from anticipation: in Arabic the phrase "Milan is a great city" does not have the verb "to be" (A1-02), and in the city there are universities, is said to be in the city, university ( ⁧فِي المَدِينَةِ جَامِعَاتٌ⁩ ).
Arabic uses two sets of digits, with the same value as ours:
Indo-Arab (Middle East) ⁧٠١٢٣٤٥٦٧٨٩⁩
• Where In the Maghreb and on many sites European figures are used; in Egypt, in the Levant, in Iraq and in the Gulf Indo-Arabs, often mixed with Europeans.
• Direction. The numbers are written and read from left to right, even in an Arabic text: ⁧٢٠٢٦⁩ =
• Persian variants. In Iran, Afghanistan and Pakistan some figures change shape ( ⁧۴⁩ , ⁧۵⁩ , ⁧۶⁩ for 4, 5, 6):
recognize them in the files of that area.

• Dates. After the year often appears ⁧م⁩ ( ⁧مِيلَادِيّ⁩ , Gregorian calendar) or ⁧هـ⁩ ( ⁧هِجْرِيّ⁩ , calendar of Egira, lunar): ⁧٢٠٢٦م⁩ ; in 2026 runs the passage between the 1447 and the 1448 of the Egira.
• Decimal separator. In Indo-Arabic numeral printing, the sign is used ⁧٫⁩ in place of the comma: ⁧٥٫٩٠⁩ =

So far you have read and written in naskh , the printwriting. By hand most Arabs write in ruqʿa , faster: you will meet her on notes, handwritten forms, letters, signs, written on the walls. How to recognize her.
• Two points become a dash; Three points a small .
• Teeth of ⁧س⁩ and ⁧ش⁩ They disappear: they become a flat line.
• The letters rest almost all on the line and are more compact; the final queues are short.
• ⁧ي⁩ final and ⁧ى⁩ They often look alike.
Font ruqʿa printed here is a good approximation; The actual handwriting of each person varies a lot. In this course the ruqʿa It is only to be recognized: write in naskh.

1. Shadowing. Listen to the phrase-by-phrase B script and repeat overlaying the voice as long as you can read together with vocal synthesis.
2. Expressive reading. Read the headlines like a radio journalist: pause after each title, related words (fi l-madīnati, ʿalā l-ḥudūdi).
3. Comparison. Record timed reading of L0-05 and compare it with the recorded one then: ⁧ح⁩ , ⁧ع⁩ , Ethical.
